title: Quarter Fabric: align hosted API sprint lanes with model-catalog commitment windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket coordinates a single, auditable quarterly plan that synchronizes hosted API sprint lanes with model-catalog commitment windows. We will produce the commitment calendar, a staggered canary schedule, explicit capacity hedges, and an evaluation/rollback playbook to reduce regressions during model rotations. The outcome should be a repeatable process that product, engineering, design, and SRE teams can follow each quarter to minimize customer impact while enabling faster model updates.
goals: 1) Publish a synchronized quarter plan that maps endpoint tiers to model-catalog commit windows. 2) Reduce model-rotation customer regressions by 40% vs last quarter. 3) Shorten cross-team decision latency for canary approvals to under 48 hours.
okrs: O1: Improve operational predictability for hosted model updates. KR1: Commit calendar published and adopted by >=90% of endpoint owners. KR2: Canary schedule executed with documented metrics for every rotation. O2: Improve model quality safety net. KR3: Integrate 2 high-value eval suites into CI for catalog onboarding.
milestones: - 2026-03-12: Kickoff + cross-functional intake workshop (complete). - 2026-03-19: Draft commitment calendar and tranche definitions (in review). - 2026-04-02: Canary schedule and SLA guardrails finalized. - 2026-04-16: Evaluation suites integrated into model onboarding CI. - 2026-05-07: Dry-run rotation with internal workloads. - 2026-05-21: Post-dry-run retro and playbook updates. - 2026-05-31: Quarter Fabric deliverables published and handoff to operations.
rollout_plan: 1) Publish calendar and playbook to Confluence + notify endpoint owners. 2) Run internal dry-run with a low-risk endpoint and verify metrics pipeline (latency, token-cost, quality regressions). 3) Execute staged canaries for one mid-volume model, collect metrics, and practice rollbacks. 4) Formalize signoff checklist and integrate into release gates for hostedapi-2026.05.
acceptance_criteria: - Commitment calendar exists and is versioned in Confluence. - Canary schedule includes cadence, success metrics, and rollback triggers. - Two eval suites are wired into model onboarding CI and run automatically. - Operations runbooks for emergency rotation and capacity hedges are documented and validated during dry-run.
risks: - Resource contention: Eng bandwidth to implement CI hooks and SRE support during canaries. - Canary signal noise: Insufficient telemetry for small changes could produce false positives. - Customer impact: Mistuned rollout windows for high-SLA endpoints. - Cross-team adoption risk if calendar is perceived as extra overhead.
mitigations: - Prioritize API telemetry instrumentation work as part of this ticket and negotiate 1 sprint of ENG scope. - Define minimal viable signal set for canaries (latency p95, error rate, quality hits on golden prompts). - Reserve a capacity hedge pool (small Dedicated allocation) for rollbacks. - Run two onboarding workshops and make calendar enforcement opt-out for first quarter with follow-up incentives.
